Presymplectic form (dω=0,rankω=constant)

Words: 68
Symplectic geometry OurBigBook.com
A presymplectic form is a closed two-form, commonly assumed to have constant rank, that need not be nondegenerate. A symplectic form is its nondegenerate special case. Its kernel distribution is integrable: for kernel fields X,Y, the identity dω=0 gives ι[X,Y]​ω=0. If the characteristic leaf quotient is smooth and the form descends, that quotient has a symplectic form. A regular Hamiltonian energy hypersurface carries such a form with kernel spanned by its Hamiltonian vector field.

Symplectic capacity (c(X,ω))

Words: 292 Articles: 4
Symplectic geometry OurBigBook.com
A symplectic capacity is monotone under symplectic embeddings, scales by c(X,aω)=ac(X,ω) for a>0, and has positive unit-ball capacity and finite unit-cylinder capacity. It is invariant under symplectomorphisms. A normalized symplectic capacity additionally assigns π to both unit domains.

Normalized symplectic capacity (c(B2n(1))=c(Z2n(1))=π)

Words: 24
Symplectic capacity OurBigBook.com
A normalized symplectic capacity has the displayed unit-ball and unit-cylinder values. Dilation gives πR2 for both radius-R domains. Monotonicity then implies the sharp Gromov non-squeezing theorem.

Eliashberg–Gromov rigidity theorem (Symp(M,ω) is C0-closed in Diff(M))

Words: 71
Symplectic capacity OurBigBook.com
A locally uniform limit of symplectomorphisms that is a smooth diffeomorphism is symplectic. By capacity preservation under uniform limits and linear capacity rigidity, its derivative is symplectic or anti-symplectic. Repeat this argument after taking the product of every map with the identity on a symplectic plane. An anti-symplectic derivative on the original factor and a symplectic derivative on the added factor would give neither sign on the product, a contradiction. The argument uses symplectic capacities in the original and stabilized dimensions.

Linear capacity rigidity (c(TE)=c(E) for all ellipsoids⟹T∗ω=±ω)

Words: 103
Symplectic capacity OurBigBook.com
An invertible real linear map preserving symplectic capacities of all solid ellipsoids is symplectic or anti-symplectic. For a pair with ω(u,v)=1, if 0<∣ω(TTu,TTv)∣<1, complete this pair and its normalized transformed pair to symplectic bases. The resulting transpose matrix sends a unit ball into a symplectic cylinder of radius less than one, contradicting the capacity axioms after iterating the resulting linear map: its first coordinate pair contracts geometrically, while the image ellipsoid retains positive capacity. Perturbation handles a zero pairing; using T−1 handles absolute value greater than one. Thus the absolute bilinear pairings agree. Their squares agree as polynomials, and the polynomial ring being an integral domain forces one global sign.

Capacity preservation under uniform limits

Words: 59
Symplectic capacity OurBigBook.com
Suppose diffeomorphisms preserving capacities of solid ellipsoids converge uniformly on compact sets to a diffeomorphism ϕ. For 0<a<1, uniform closeness and degree of a continuous mapping give ϕj​(aE)⊆ϕ(E)⊆ϕj​(a−1E). The capacity axioms squeeze c(ϕ(E)) between a2c(E) and a−2c(E). Letting a tend to one proves equality. Rescaling a smooth ϕ near a point and repeating the argument also proves capacity preservation by its derivative.

Geometric quantization

Words: 415 Articles: 6
Symplectic geometry OurBigBook.com
Geometric quantization associates quantum states and observables with a symplectic manifold. A first step uses a complex line bundle with a connection on a vector bundle whose curvature is proportional to the symplectic form divided by ℏ; its existence imposes an integrality condition. A real polarization is an integrable half-dimensional distribution with Lagrangian submanifolds as leaves. Requiring sections to be covariantly constant along the leaves reduces the variables to a configuration-space description. Restricting the curvature to a Lagrangian leaf gives zero, permitting local flat sections; global sections can require trivial holonomy. Exact Lagrangian graphs also describe local semiclassical phases through their generating functions.

Polarization in geometric quantization (F⊂TC​P)

Words: 194 Articles: 2
Geometric quantization OurBigBook.com
A polarization is an involutive complex rank-half distribution on which the symplectic form vanishes. Polarized prequantum sections satisfy ∇X​s=0 for X∈F. A real polarization is tangent to a Lagrangian foliation; a complex Kähler polarization uses the antiholomorphic tangent spaces. Only observables whose Hamiltonian flows preserve the chosen distribution act directly on the polarized space. Singular leaves, holonomy and changes of polarization are genuine quantization difficulties.

Blattner-Kostant-Sternberg pairing

Words: 77
Polarization in geometric quantization OurBigBook.com
The pairing compares state spaces belonging to two polarizations using their prequantum sections and half-forms. When it defines a suitable identification or projection, a classical Hamiltonian flow can transport a state to its transported polarization and the pairing can return it to the original state space. Differentiating this construction supplies operators for some observables that do not directly preserve the original polarization. Existence, domains and unitarity require additional hypotheses; it is not a universal canonical equivalence of all polarizations.

Metaplectic correction

Words: 57
Polarization in geometric quantization OurBigBook.com
Tensor the prequantum bundle with a square root of the canonical determinant bundle of a polarization, when such a square root exists. The half-form contributes to the state pairing and to the observable action. It improves coordinate invariance and accounts for familiar Maslov and oscillator zero-point shifts. Its existence is additional global data, not automatic from prequantum integrality.

Prequantization ([ω/(2πℏ)]∈H2(P,Z))

Words: 129 Articles: 2
Geometric quantization OurBigBook.com
Prequantization realizes a symplectic manifold using a Hermitian line bundle with connection whose curvature is iω/ℏ in the convention ιXf​​ω=df. Its existence requires integral symplectic periods. On sections, the Kostant-Souriau prequantum operator represents every classical observable and its Poisson bracket, but the resulting states depend on the full phase space. A polarization in geometric quantization removes this excess of variables.

Kostant-Souriau prequantum operator (f​=−iℏ∇Xf​​+f)

Words: 35
Prequantization OurBigBook.com
For ιXf​​ω=df and F∇​=iω/ℏ, the curvature commutator and [Xf​,Xg​]=−X{f,g}​ give [f​,g​]=iℏ{f,g}​. In cotangent coordinates, θ=pdq gives f​=−iℏXf​+f−θ(Xf​). Restriction to a vertical polarization yields q​=q and p​=−iℏ∂q​.

Prequantum line bundle (F∇​=iω/ℏ)

Words: 46
Prequantization OurBigBook.com
A prequantum line bundle is a Hermitian line bundle over a symplectic manifold with unitary connection on a vector bundle of the displayed curvature. With ω=−dθ, a local connection is ∇=d−iθ/ℏ. Reversing the Hamiltonian-vector-field convention or passing to the dual line bundle reverses the corresponding curvature convention. Integrality of ω/(2πℏ) on closed two-cycles is the topological existence condition.

Hamiltonian group action

Words: 819 Articles: 14
Symplectic geometry OurBigBook.com
A Hamiltonian group action is a Lie group action on a symplectic manifold with an equivariant moment map μ:M→g∗. In the sign convention ιXH​​ω=dH, each component satisfies d⟨μ,X⟩=ιXM​​ω, where XM​ is the fundamental vector field. The opposite Hamiltonian vector field convention reverses the sign.

Weakly Hamiltonian action

Words: 101 Articles: 1
Hamiltonian group action OurBigBook.com
A symplectic Lie group action is weakly Hamiltonian when every fundamental vector field is a Hamiltonian vector field. A Hamiltonian group action additionally supplies Hamiltonians as components of an equivariant moment map. Constants in the component Hamiltonians do not affect their vector fields, but the ability to choose them with the required equivariance is an additional global condition.

Hamiltonian existence for a semisimple symplectic action ([g,g]=g)

Words: 56
Weakly Hamiltonian action OurBigBook.com
For a symplectic left Lie group action, use actual fundamental fields ξP​ and ιXf​​ω=df. They satisfy [ξP​,ηP​]=−[ξ,η]P​. Cartan's magic formula then gives ι[ξ,η]P​​ω=d[ω(ξP​,ηP​)]. Thus every commutator generator has a globally exact contraction. A semisimple Lie algebra is perfect, so every generator has a global Hamiltonian. The separate semisimple moment-map equivariance result removes the constant two-cocycle obstruction and gives an equivariant moment map for a connected group.

Symplectic reduction (μ−1(c)/G)

Words: 276 Articles: 4
Hamiltonian group action OurBigBook.com
For a Hamiltonian group action, a regular value level preserved by a free proper group action has a smooth quotient. The restricted symplectic form descends to a symplectic form on that quotient when the kernel is exactly the orbit directions; this is symplectic reduction.

Lagrangian lift through circle reduction (L=π−1(L))

Words: 58
Symplectic reduction OurBigBook.com
At a regular free circle group level of a moment map, the inverse image of a Lagrangian submanifold of the reduced space is a Lagrangian submanifold of the original space. Its restricted symplectic form is the pullback of the reduced form and hence vanishes. Its dimension is one more than that of the reduced Lagrangian, exactly half the ambient dimension. It is a circle bundle over the original Lagrangian.

Planar rotational symplectic reduction (ωred​=dr∧dpr​)

Words: 46
Symplectic reduction OurBigBook.com
For a planar cotangent bundle, rotation has moment map ℓ=xpy​−ypx​. At ℓ=0 its level is regular and the circle action is free. Polar canonical coordinates give ω=dr∧dpr​+dθ∧dℓ. Fixing ℓ and quotienting θ leaves T∗R>0​ with the displayed form. The unit-mass free Hamiltonian becomes pr2​/2+ℓ2/(2r2).

Symplectic reduction of an isotropic oscillator (H−1(E)/S1≅CPn−1)

Words: 58
Symplectic reduction OurBigBook.com
For H=∑j​(qj2​+pj2​)/2 and E>0, the oscillator flow is a free circle action on the sphere of radius 2E​. Its quotient is Complex projective space. For two modes, the reduced form in w=z2​/z1​ is iEdw∧dwˉ/(1+∣w∣2)2, of total area 2πE. Reduction at zero energy is singular instead of a smooth quotient of the asserted dimension.

Marsden-Weinstein theorem (μ−1(c)/G)

Words: 80
Symplectic reduction OurBigBook.com
For a Hamiltonian group action, let c be a regular value of the moment map fixed by the coadjoint action, and assume the action on μ−1(c) is free and proper. The quotient is a symplectic manifold of dimension dimM−2dimG. Its unique reduced symplectic form is characterized by π∗ωc​=ι∗ω, where ι includes the level set and π is the quotient projection. The kernel of the restricted two-form consists precisely of the orbit directions. More general noncentral levels use their stabilizer group; the stated central-level version suffices for circle group reduction.

Restriction of a Hamiltonian group action

Words: 18
Hamiltonian group action OurBigBook.com
Restriction to a Lie subgroup with Lie algebra inclusion i:h→g has moment map i∗μ. The dual map i∗ composes with the original moment map.

Moment map (μ:M→g∗)

Words: 388 Articles: 5
Hamiltonian group action OurBigBook.com
A moment map assigns to each element of a Lie algebra a Hamiltonian function for its fundamental vector field, and is equivariant for the coadjoint action. For an abelian Lie group, constant shifts are allowed; the numerical scale also depends on the chosen Lie algebra generators and the normalization of the symplectic form.

Unitary moment map of an isotropic oscillator (μA​=z†Az,z=(x+ip)/2​)

Words: 68
Moment map OurBigBook.com
On the canonical cotangent bundle T∗Rn, ω=i∑dzj​∧dzˉj​ and H=z†z. The unitary group acts by z↦Uz, preserving both. For a Hermitian A, the generator −iA has Hamiltonian μA​=z†Az. The Poisson bracket satisfies {μA​,μB​}=μ−i[A,B]​, with no central term. The central generator has moment map H; imaginary antisymmetric matrices give ordinary angular momentum, while real symmetric matrices give quadratic observables mixing position and momentum.

Moment-map equivariance obstruction (κ(X,Y)={μX​,μY​}−μ[X,Y]​)

Words: 207 Articles: 2
Moment map OurBigBook.com
For a weakly Hamiltonian left Lie group action on a connected symplectic manifold, choose ιXf​​ω=df. Fundamental vector fields and Hamiltonian vector fields are both antihomomorphisms, so the displayed difference is constant. The Jacobi identity for the Poisson bracket makes it a two-cocycle. Changing μX​ by b(X) changes the difference by −b([X,Y]). Thus its class in Lie algebra cohomology obstructs choosing an equivariant moment map. For a connected group, vanishing of this class gives infinitesimal and group equivariance.
Fixed-point normalization removes the moment-map cocycle ({μξ​,μη​}=μ[ξ,η]​)
Words: 93
Moment-map equivariance obstruction OurBigBook.com
Suppose a symplectic Lie group action on a connected symplectic manifold has global component Hamiltonians and a common fixed point p0​. Choose their constants linearly so μξ​(p0​)=0. The difference c(ξ,η)={μξ​,μη​}−μ[ξ,η]​ has zero Hamiltonian vector field because fundamental fields and Hamiltonian fields have compatible Lie-bracket conventions; it is therefore constant. At p0​, all fundamental fields vanish, so both terms in c vanish. Thus c=0 everywhere and the Poisson brackets of the components reproduce the group Lie algebra. For a connected group this also yields coadjoint equivariance. A linear unitary action on a vector space has the origin as such a fixed point.
Semisimple moment-map equivariance (H2(g,R)=0)
Words: 56
Moment-map equivariance obstruction OurBigBook.com
For a semisimple Lie algebra, its nondegenerate Killing form turns a two-cocycle into an operator D through B(DX,Y)=κ(X,Y). The cocycle identity makes D a derivation. Choose Z by B(Z,X)=tr(DadX). Using [D,adX]=ad(DX) and cyclicity of trace gives B([Z,X],Y)=B(DX,Y), so D=adZ. Consequently κ(X,Y)=B(Z,[X,Y]) is a coboundary. This proves that component Hamiltonians can be normalized to a Lie algebra homomorphism.

Moment map for rotation of the complex projective line (H(z)=∣z∣2/(1+∣z∣2))

Words: 71
Moment map OurBigBook.com
For the symplectic form ω=idz∧dzˉ/(1+∣z∣2)2, the circle group rotates z by eiθ. Its real generator is K=iz∂z​−izˉ∂zˉ​. The contraction is ιK​ω=−dH, so H is a Hamiltonian function in this sign convention. In the other chart w=1/z, H=1/(1+∣w∣2), proving smoothness at infinity. Its image is [0,1] with the endpoints at the fixed poles. The symplectic area is 2π; rescaling to the round area 4π would double this moment function.

Anti-symplectic map

Words: 60 Articles: 2
Symplectic geometry OurBigBook.com
An anti-symplectic map between symplectic manifolds is a diffeomorphism f satisfying f∗ω′=−ω. For symplectic vector spaces, the analogous definition uses an invertible linear map.

Anti-symplectic involution (σ2=I, σ∗ω=−ω)

Words: 41 Articles: 1
Anti-symplectic map OurBigBook.com
An anti-symplectic involution is an anti-symplectic map whose square is the identity. Its nonempty fixed-point set is a Lagrangian submanifold; the linear version has complementary +1 and −1 Lagrangian subspaces.

Lagrangian fixed locus of an anti-symplectic involution

Words: 17
Anti-symplectic involution OurBigBook.com
A nonempty fixed-point set of an anti-symplectic involution is a Lagrangian submanifold. Local linearization identifies its tangent space with the +1 eigenspace of the derivative.

Symplectic group (Sp(2n,R))

Words: 443 Articles: 9
Symplectic geometry OurBigBook.com
The real symplectic group consists of matrices A satisfying ATJA=J. It is an embedded matrix Lie group of dimension 2n2+n in size 2n.

Symplectic group over a field (Sp(V,B))

Words: 51
Symplectic group OurBigBook.com
For a finite-dimensional vector space over any field with a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form B, the symplectic group over a field consists of invertible linear maps preserving B. In a symplectic basis its matrices satisfy gTJg=J. Matching two symplectic bases gives a unique such linear map, and a symplectic basis exists by successively splitting off paired vectors. This includes arbitrary-characteristic and infinite-field versions, beyond the real Lie group and the symplectic group over a finite field.

Symplectic matrix (ATJA=J)

Words: 32
Symplectic group OurBigBook.com
An invertible real matrix preserving the standard symplectic form. With J=(0−I​I0​), it satisfies ATJA=J, equivalently AJAT=J. The first identity describes preservation of the form; the second describes preservation of coordinate Poisson brackets.

Symplectic parabolic subgroup

Words: 247 Articles: 3
Symplectic group OurBigBook.com
The stabilizer of a totally isotropic k-space in a finite symplectic space also stabilizes its orthogonal complement. Its block decomposition has a unipotent normal subgroup Q and a block-diagonal complement L≅GLk​(q)×Sp2m−2k​(q). The paired k-space carries the contragredient action. A row-vector convention gives upper-triangular blocks; a column-vector convention transposes the arrangement. The unipotent radical count for a symplectic parabolic subgroup yields its order.

Symplectic Lagrangian stabilizer (Pm​=Symm​(q)⋊GLm​(q))

Words: 45
Symplectic parabolic subgroup OurBigBook.com
With a Lagrangian subspace first in a paired symplectic basis, its stabilizer consists of (A0​ASA−T​) with S symmetric. The additive symmetric-matrix unipotent radical has order qm(m+1)/2; the Levi subgroup is GLm​(q), acting by S↦ASAT. Its index in Sp2m​(q) is ∏i=1m​(qi+1), the number of Lagrangian subspaces.

Symplectic point stabilizer (P1​=U⋊(Fq×​×Sp2m−2​(q)))

Words: 74
Symplectic parabolic subgroup OurBigBook.com
For a line ⟨e⟩, complete (e,f) to a symplectic basis with complementary symplectic space W. The unipotent radical has elements u(b,t) sending e to e, w to w−B(w,b)e and f to f+b+te. Its multiplication is (b,t)(b′,t′)=(b+b′,t+t′+B(b,b′)), giving order q2m−1. Its commutator is central with parameter 2B(b,b′). This first-order operator vanishes exactly on J-holomorphic curves. Linearization at a map u gives a Fredholm operator between suitable Sobolev spaces of sections. At a constant map it is the Dolbeault operator on the trivial pulled-back tangent bundle.

Cauchy–Riemann operator OurBigBook.com
A real-linear Cauchy–Riemann operator on a complex rank-n vector bundle over a closed genus-g Riemann surface is a Fredholm operator between the usual Sobolev spaces and has the displayed index. Zero-order real-linear terms do not change this index, since they form a continuous deformation of Fredholm operators. For the bundle pulled back by a sphere, subtracting the six-dimensional reparametrization group gives the dimension formula for regular J-holomorphic spheres.
Regularity of a J-holomorphic curve (Du​ is surjective)

Cauchy–Riemann operator OurBigBook.com
A J-holomorphic curve is regular when the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective. Regularity only for simple curves is weaker than regularity for all maps: multiple covers of an exceptional sphere can fail regularity even when that simple sphere is regular.
Generic transversality for simple holomorphic spheres
Words: 68
Regularity of a J-holomorphic curve OurBigBook.com
For a residual set of smooth compatible almost complex structures, all simple J-holomorphic spheres in a specified countable set of spherical classes are regular. The corresponding evaluation maps at marked points are transverse to generic incidence conditions; generic paths give parameterized transversality. The universal linearization can vary the target structure near an injective point of the curve, which removes its cokernel. This assertion concerns simple curves and does not ensure regularity of arbitrary multiple covers.
Negative-square exclusion under full sphere regularity
Words: 83
Regularity of a J-holomorphic curve OurBigBook.com
If every nonconstant J-holomorphic sphere under consideration is regular, no such sphere in a four-dimensional target has class A with A2≤−2. For a simple J-holomorphic sphere, the adjunction inequality for a simple J-holomorphic sphere makes the predicted moduli dimension negative. A degree-m multiple cover of class B has B2≤−1 and c1​(B)≤1, so its predicted real dimension is at most 2m−2. The rational covering maps of the projective line already form a family of dimension 4m−4>2m−2, contradicting regularity. The full regularity hypothesis matters: multiple covers of exceptional minus-one spheres violate the conclusion under a simple-only regularity assumption.

Arbitrarily large symplectic balls in a cotangent cylinder

Words: 49
Non-squeezing theorem OurBigBook.com
The symplectic manifold T2×R2 contains symplectic balls of arbitrarily large radius. A steep linear Lagrangian graph in R4=T∗R2 has a thin neighborhood that injects under the quotient R2→T2, while a symplectic base-fiber dilation fits a large round ball into that long thin neighborhood.

Symplectic fiber sum along a square-zero surface

Words: 42
Symplectic manifold OurBigBook.com
If symplectic four-manifolds contain symplectic copies of the same closed surface with self-intersection zero, their trivial symplectic normal bundles may be identified with reversed circle fibers. Removing the two tubular neighborhoods and gluing their boundaries gives a symplectic sum carrying a natural symplectic form.

Gompf realization theorem

Words: 60
Symplectic manifold OurBigBook.com
Every finitely presented group is the fundamental group of a closed symplectic four-manifold. The construction starts from products of surfaces, realizes relator words by embedded loops after stabilization, and takes symplectic sums with copies of the rational elliptic surface along square-zero tori. Since the complement of a regular elliptic fiber in the rational elliptic surface is simply connected, van Kampen's theorem imposes the desired generators and relators.

The Gromov width of a symplectic manifold is the supremum of πr2 over radii of symplectically embedded balls B2n(r).

Words: 46
Gromov width OurBigBook.com
When each projective line has area π, the product CP1×CP1 has Gromov width π. The lower bound comes from the product of two area-π discs; the upper bound comes from a J-holomorphic sphere of area π through the center of any proposed ball.

Liouville class of a Lagrangian submanifold ([λ∣L​])

Words: 248 Articles: 3
Symplectic manifold OurBigBook.com
For a Lagrangian submanifold L⊂(R2n,dλ), the restriction λ∣L​ is closed. Its cohomology class is preserved by ambient symplectomorphisms because every closed one-form on R2n is exact. On a product torus of circles, its periods are the enclosed symplectic areas of the factors.

Holomorphic disk detects a nonzero Liouville class

Words: 59
Liouville class of a Lagrangian submanifold OurBigBook.com
For a smooth nonconstant holomorphic disk h in Cn with boundary on a Lagrangian submanifold L, its symplectic area is ∫D2​∣∂s​h∣2dsdt>0. The Cauchy-Riemann equations give ∂t​h=J∂s​h, so this is the pullback of the standard symplectic form. The Stokes theorem identifies the area with the period of a primitive along the boundary loop. Thus the Liouville class of a Lagrangian submanifold evaluates nontrivially on this loop and cannot vanish.

Rational Lagrangian submanifold

Words: 144 Articles: 1
Liouville class of a Lagrangian submanifold OurBigBook.com
For a Lagrangian submanifold L in an exact symplectic manifold with primitive λ, its period subgroup is {∫c​λ:c∈H1​(L;Z)}⊂R. It is rational when this subgroup is discrete. If it is nonzero, it is γZ for a unique γ>0. Some conventions reserve the word rational for this nonzero case. The zero subgroup corresponds to an exact differential form λ∣L​; its least positive period is interpreted as +∞ if that endpoint convention is admitted.
Least positive Liouville period (γ(L)=inf{a>0:a∈Per(L)})
Words: 70
Rational Lagrangian submanifold OurBigBook.com
For a nonzero discrete Liouville period group, this is its positive generator. In Euclidean symplectic space, the same group is obtained from signed symplectic areas of disks with boundary on L, by the Stokes theorem and contractibility of the ambient space. A product of circles of common radius r is a rational Lagrangian submanifold with γ(L)=πr2. Translation changes a primitive only by an exact form and hence leaves the period group unchanged.
